content.text: {"primary_meaning":"The visible outcome or evidence produced by a person’s inner spiritual condition—especially character, conduct, and good works. In Christian teaching, “good fruit” commonly denotes righteousness and the virtues produced by the Holy Spirit, while “bad fruit” denotes sinful conduct revealing a corrupt source.","primary_basis":["Matthew 7:16–20 — people, especially false prophets, are known by their fruits.","Luke 6:43–45 — good or evil fruit proceeds from the corresponding condition of the heart.","Galatians 5:22–23 — the fruit of the Spirit is expressed in virtues such as love, joy, peace, and self-control.","John 15:1–8, 16 — abiding in Christ results in bearing much fruit.","Matthew 3:8–10; Luke 3:8–9 — fruit serves as evidence of genuine repentance.","Philippians 1:11 — believers are to be filled with the fruit of righteousness.","Colossians 1:10 — a worthy life bears fruit in every good work."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"People brought to faith or the results of evangelism and ministry.","basis":["John 4:35–38 — harvest imagery is applied to gathering people.","Romans 1:13 — Paul desires fruit among the Roman believers or converts.","1 Corinthians 3:6–9 — planting and growth describe ministerial results."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Praise, worship, charitable giving, or other particular offerings made to God.","basis":["Hebrews 13:15 — praise is called the fruit of lips that confess God’s name.","Philippians 4:17 — financial support is described as fruit credited to the giver.","Romans 15:28 — the Gentile contribution is described metaphorically as fruit."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Human offspring or descendants, especially in the expression “fruit of the womb.”","basis":["Psalm 127:3 — children are the fruit of the womb.","Luke 1:42 — Jesus is called the fruit of Mary’s womb.","Deuteronomy 28:4, 11 — fruit of the womb denotes offspring within covenant blessing."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The consequences or recompense of one’s choices and deeds—beneficial or destructive.","basis":["Proverbs 1:31 — people eat the fruit of their way.","Proverbs 12:14; 13:2 — a person is satisfied by the fruit of speech or conduct.","Hosea 10:13 — wickedness produces its corresponding fruit.","Romans 6:21–22 — sinful and sanctified lives yield contrasting fruit and outcomes."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Agricultural abundance, fertility, and covenant blessing, sometimes contrasted with barrenness or judgment.","basis":["Deuteronomy 28:4, 11, 18, 33 — produce and fertility signify blessing or curse.","Psalm 1:3 — the righteous person resembles a tree yielding fruit in season.","Micah 4:4; Amos 9:13–14 — agricultural flourishing accompanies restoration."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"In Edenic interpretation, the forbidden fruit symbolizes disobedience, illicitly seized knowledge, temptation, or humanity’s attempt at moral autonomy.","basis":["Genesis 2:16–17; 3:1–7 — eating the forbidden fruit constitutes the primal transgression.","Romans 5:12–19 — later Christian interpretation relates Adam’s disobedience to sin and death, though it does not focus on the fruit as an independent symbol."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Eschatological life, healing, and restored communion with God, especially the fruit of the tree of life.","basis":["Genesis 2:9; 3:22–24 — the tree of life and its fruit are associated with enduring life.","Revelation 2:7 — the victorious are granted access to the tree of life.","Revelation 22:1–2, 14 — the tree’s fruit and leaves appear in the restored creation."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a strong conventional meaning when “fruit” is used morally or spiritually: observable character, deeds, and outcomes reveal and arise from an underlying spiritual source. However, the Bible uses the image in several well-established ways, so the term by itself has no single settled symbolic interpretation apart from context."}
